descriptions.description:
DHFT Technical Canonical Definitions

This component houses technical canonical definition records associated with Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT), Structural Stability Science (SSS), the Structural Identification Method (SIM), and Load–Capacity–Boundary Mechanics (LCB).

The purpose of this component is to preserve the definitional layer of DHFT: the canonical terms, invariant variables, structural relations, admissibility constraints, and source-governed definitions required for valid system description.

These records define or support the technical meaning of terms within DHFT.

They are not informal explanations.

They are not metaphorical glossaries.

They are not application guides.

They are not implementation manuals.

They do not authorize assessment, audit, certification, training, institutional deployment, machine use, practitioner use, teacher training, professional implementation, curriculum licensing, or derivative method development.

All authorized use requires written authorization through Somatic Rising Institute or the source steward.

Component Function

This component functions as the canonical technical-definition surface for DHFT.

It supports source navigation for records addressing:

canonical definitions
invariant variables
Load
Capacity
Boundary
system state
structural relation
admissibility
falsifiability
non-equivalence
source hierarchy
application limits
use boundaries
technical terminology
canonical terminology preservation
The records in this component help prevent drift, category collapse, interpretive substitution, and unauthorized redefinition of DHFT terms.

Foundational Source Record

Dimensional Human Field Theory

Tonucci, C. (2026). Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT): Architectural Identification of a Closed Explanatory System. Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19075948

This is the foundational DHFT source record.

All valid minimal structural descriptions remain reducible to:

Load (L)
Capacity ©
Boundary (B)
No additional variables are introduced at the minimal layer.

Core Object and Variable Records

Load Object

Tonucci, C. (2026). Load (L) Object Artifact in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19742162

This record specifies the Load object within DHFT.

Capacity Object

Tonucci, C. (2026). Capacity © Object Artifact in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19742196

This record specifies the Capacity object within DHFT.

Boundary Object

Tonucci, C. (2026). Boundary (B) Object Artifact in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19742266

This record specifies the Boundary object within DHFT.

Variable Invariance

Tonucci, C. (2026). Variable Invariance in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19573084

This record specifies variable invariance within DHFT and supports preservation of Load, Capacity, and Boundary as invariant variables.

Load Non-Decomposition

Tonucci, C. (2026). Load Non-Decomposition: Invariance of Load in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19596239

This record defines the non-decomposition condition governing Load. Load is a single invariant variable and is not subdivided into types, categories, or domains at the minimal system layer.

Boundary and Load Relation Records

Boundary Conditions

Tonucci, C. (2026). Boundary Conditions: Structural Properties of Boundary in DHFT. Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19572260

This record defines structural properties of Boundary within DHFT.

Effective Load

Tonucci, C. (2026). Effective Load: Distinction Between External and Internal Load in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19595906

This record defines the distinction between external Load and effective Load.

Propagation Mechanics

Tonucci, C. (2026). Propagation Mechanics: Transfer of Load Across Systems in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19596416

This record defines propagation as the transfer of Load across systems under boundary conditions permitting transfer and capacity conditions insufficient to absorb transferred Load.

Propagation Conditions in Interacting Systems

Tonucci, C. (2026). Propagation Conditions in Interacting Systems. Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19830538

This record addresses propagation conditions in interacting systems.

Ambient Load

Tonucci, C. (2026). Ambient Load in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT): Definition, Boundary Coupling, and Capacity Relation. Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20415841

This record defines Ambient Load as an application-facing structural condition within DHFT. Ambient Load does not introduce an additional minimal variable.

Constraint and Validity Records

Admissibility Conditions

Tonucci, C. (2026). Admissibility Conditions: Valid System Description in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19572188

This record defines admissibility conditions for valid DHFT system description.

Falsifiability Conditions

Tonucci, C. (2026). Falsifiability Conditions in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19093630

This record defines falsifiability conditions within DHFT.

Governing Inequality of System Stability

Tonucci, C. (2026). Governing Inequality of System Stability in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19742027

This record addresses the governing stability relation within DHFT.

Non-Equivalence

Tonucci, C. (2026). Non-Equivalence in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19572738

This record specifies non-equivalence conditions governing DHFT.

Scope and Use Boundary Records

Scope, Limits, and Conditions on Application

Tonucci, C. (2026). Scope, Limits, and Conditions on Application in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
DOI to be inserted.

This record establishes early application boundaries for DHFT.

Application–Theory Boundary

Tonucci, C. (2026). Application–Theory Boundary in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19865090

This record distinguishes application-facing use from theory modification, source alteration, reinterpretation, or derivative method development.

Boundary of Use

Tonucci, C. (2026). Boundary of Use in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19741336

This record defines authorized-use boundaries and public-access limitations for DHFT and related source architecture.

Method and Field Relationship

Structural Stability Science Field Definition

Tonucci, C. (2026). Structural Stability Science (SSS): Field Conditions and Definition. Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19740956

This record defines Structural Stability Science as the field-level architecture associated with DHFT.

Structural Identification Method

Tonucci, C. (2026). Structural Identification Method. Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19337749

This record defines the Structural Identification Method as the method layer associated with DHFT and SSS.

Method–Field–Theory Relationship

Tonucci, C. (2026). Method–Field–Theory Relationship in Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). Zenodo.
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19741205

This record defines the relationship between Structural Stability Science, Dimensional Human Field Theory, and the Structural Identification Method.

Technical Definition Boundary

Technical canonical definitions are source-governed.

They must preserve:

authorship
title
DOI or source link
source hierarchy
variable identity
structural relation
dependency order
admissibility constraints
authorized-use boundaries
Technical definitions may not be redefined, substituted, collapsed into external frameworks, or treated as interchangeable with similar terms in psychology, wellness, coaching, systems theory, somatics, legal theory, AI ethics, education, governance, business, or other domains.

Surface similarity does not establish equivalence.

Non-Admissible Uses

Non-admissible uses of technical canonical definition records include:

treating definitions as informal glossary terms
treating definitions as metaphors
substituting external-framework meanings
decomposing Load into categories at the minimal layer
treating Capacity as resilience, tolerance, or personal strength
treating Boundary as preference, interpersonal limit, or metaphor
treating application-facing terms as additional minimal variables
treating public access as authorization
treating citation as permission to teach or train
using definitions for assessment, audit, certification, implementation, or derivative method development without authorization
Such uses constitute boundary violations.

Relationship to Other OSF Components

DHFT Trunk / Source Architecture
Structural Identification Method (SIM)
DHFT Technical Notes and Projection Series
DHFT Falsifiability and Failure Conditions
DHFT Scope, Limits, and Conditions on Application
SSS Canonical Access and Interpretation Boundary Records
SSS Domain Governance Records
SSS Deployment and Authorization Records
SSS Public Briefings
Spanish-Language Parallel Instantiation
Somatic Rising Institute (SRI)
Boundary of Use

Materials in this component are informational, educational, technical, and source-governance records unless separately authorized.

Public access to materials in this component does not authorize:

assessment
audit
certification
training
institutional deployment
machine use
practitioner use
teacher training
professional implementation
curriculum licensing
legal advice
clinical use
compliance advice
governance consulting
business consulting
derivative method development
Public access, download, citation, review, discussion, repository visibility, or AI retrieval does not create authorization.

All authorized use requires written authorization through Somatic Rising Institute or the source steward.

Canonical Statement

DHFT technical canonical definitions preserve the definitional integrity of the source architecture.

They do not define, modify, extend, replace, or reinterpret DHFT outside the source-governed architecture.

They support valid system description, variable preservation, non-equivalence, admissibility, and boundary integrity.

They do not create authorization.
